local_market_longform:
Kennewick is its own market, and a cash sale here works differently than the national talking points suggest. Homes in Kennewick currently trade around a median of $440,000 and take roughly 34 days to go under contract, with about 21% of area sales closing in cash. When you need certainty instead of a drawn-out listing — a firm number and a date you choose — that local pace is exactly why selling directly makes sense.

The housing stock shapes everything about condition here. Kennewick runs heavily to 1950s–1970s ranch homes near the river and newer stucco builds out toward Southridge, and each era carries its own repair realities. That matters because we price the house in front of us rather than asking you to renovate it first — the things a traditional buyer's inspector flags are the same things we already expect and account for.

Local conditions are the other factor a generic buyer ignores. Around Kennewick, the issues we see most are expansive caliche and silt soils that stress slabs and foundations, aging evaporative coolers, and irrigation-related grading issues. We've made offers on homes with every one of those problems, so none of it scares us off or kills the deal at the last minute.

We buy across the whole area — from close-in neighborhoods like Southridge out to Richland and Pasco — and in Washington the local economy anchored by Hanford site operations, PNNL, agriculture, and a growing wine industry keeps demand real. Inherited homes, tired rentals, pre-foreclosure situations in Benton County, and houses that simply need more work than the owner wants to take on: those are the Kennewick sellers we help most.

Being a genuinely local buyer near Columbia Park along the river also means our offer isn't a lowball pulled from a national algorithm that has never seen Kennewick. We know what a block in Southridge, Canyon Lakes, Zintel Canyon, and downtown Kennewick actually sells for, what the Tri-Cities buyers will and won't pay for, and how Benton County's title and closing process really works. That local read is why our sellers get a number they can trust and a closing that actually happens on the date we promised.

faq.q: How fast can you close on my Kennewick house?
faq.a: As little as 7 days through a licensed Washington title company, or any later date you choose. Sellers in Kennewick pick the timeline that fits their move.

faq.q: Do I pay any fees or commissions?
faq.a: None. No agent commissions, no listing fees, and we cover standard closing costs. The number we agree on is what you receive.

faq.q: Do I need to repair or clean the house first?
faq.a: No. We buy Kennewick homes in any condition — including the expansive caliche and silt soils that stress slabs and foundations we see so often here. Take what you want and leave the rest.

faq.q: How do you decide the offer amount?
faq.a: We look at recent comparable sales in your Kennewick neighborhood — places like Southridge — the home's condition, and current the Tri-Cities demand, then make a fair cash offer you're free to accept or decline.

faq.q: Is this a licensed, legitimate way to sell in Washington?
faq.a: Yes. We are a direct buyer, not your agent or broker, and we put that in writing. Washington has no wholesaling-specific statute; we operate as a direct buyer and disclose our interest in writing.

faq.q: Can you help with foreclosure, probate, or tenants?
faq.a: Often, yes. We regularly work with Benton County sellers facing foreclosure, probate, liens, or tenant issues, and we structure the sale around the situation.
